observations.text: SP, due to a late start of the descent that compressed the arrival profile, did not establish the aircraft at pattern altitude and briefed entry airspeed before the initial point, with the result of deviations of 400 feet and 25 knots, both beyond the +/-300 feet and +/-20 knots limits. The IP directed the level-off and the power reduction and executed part of the traffic pattern entry, as SP could not complete the VFR arrival safely without assistance.

SP, due to loss of situational awareness of the aircraft's position in the pattern, did not fly the briefed arrival leg toward the initial point and misidentified the runway in use, with the result of an entry heading error of 18 degrees, beyond the +/-10 degrees limit. The IP directed the repositioning and the sequencing with the traffic already established, so that a safe traffic pattern entry was achieved only with assistance.

SP, due to a descent rate that was not reduced before the level-off, did not arrest the descent at pattern altitude prior to traffic pattern entry, with the result of a deviation of 300 feet, at the +/-300 feet limit. The deviation was recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts, with delay.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during a critical phase of flight, did not maintain the briefed heading toward the initial point of the VFR arrival, with the result of a heading deviation of 10 degrees, at the +/-10 degrees limit. Airspeed at the same time reached 20 knots above the briefed entry speed. Both deviations were corrected only after the IP's verbal indications and with delay.

SP entered the traffic pattern at home base safely and within the desired standards, without IP's intervention. However, the arrival was stabilized late, altitude reached 200 feet and airspeed 15 knots from the briefed values on the entry leg, and both were corrected in a timely manner by SP. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier configuration and a more consistent altitude and airspeed cross-check on the arrival are expected to improve.

SP planned and executed the VFR arrival accurately and promptly, joining the traffic pattern with altitude held within 100 feet, airspeed within 8 knots and entry heading within 4 degrees, without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP conducted the VFR arrival with exceptional precision, overflying the arrival points within 0.5 NM and entering the traffic pattern with altitude held within 50 feet, airspeed within 5 knots and entry heading within 2 degrees. Radio calls, sequencing with the traffic already in the pattern and the descent profile were managed without any prompt from the IP, well above the desired levels. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect computation of the descent point for the VFR arrival, did not reach the initial point at pattern altitude and briefed entry airspeed, with the result of a 500 feet altitude excess and 30 knots above the briefed speed, both beyond the +/-300 feet and +/-20 knots limits. The IP directed the corrective descent and executed part of the traffic pattern entry to preserve separation from the traffic already established.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, did not complete the arrival checks or confirm the runway in use before reaching the initial point, with the result of an entry heading error of 20 degrees and a converging track with the downwind traffic. The IP took over the sequencing and directed the traffic pattern entry, as the VFR arrival could not be completed without assistance.

SP, due to a power setting held too high throughout the descent, did not decelerate to the briefed entry airspeed before the initial point, with the result of a deviation of 20 knots, at the +/-20 knots limit. The excess airspeed was recognized and reduced only after the IP's verbal prompts, with delay.

SP, due to an incomplete mental model of the approach sequence that was not updated when the clearance changed, did not adjust the VFR arrival to the newly assigned runway, with the result of an entry heading deviation of 10 degrees, at the +/-10 degrees limit. Pattern altitude at the same time was exceeded by 300 feet. Both deviations were corrected only after the IP's verbal indications and with delay.

SP, due to a late reduction of the descent rate before the level-off, overshot pattern altitude by 200 feet on the entry leg, a deviation between the +/-150 feet and +/-300 feet limits. The error was recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention, and the entry into the traffic pattern remained safe.

SP, due to inadequate monitoring of airspeed during the approach, did not hold the briefed entry speed for the traffic pattern, with the result of a deviation of 15 knots, between the +/-10 knots and +/-20 knots limits. The deviation was recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention.

SP executed the VFR arrival and entered the traffic pattern safely and within the desired standards, holding pattern altitude within 150 feet, entry airspeed within 10 knots and entry heading within 5 degrees, without IP's intervention. However, the parameters were held at the edge of the desired band and two corrections were required on the entry leg. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a tighter altitude and airspeed cross-check during the arrival is expected to improve.

SP executed the VFR arrival with exceptional precision, overflying the arrival points within 0.5 NM and entering the traffic pattern with altitude held within 50 feet, airspeed within 5 knots and entry heading within 2 degrees. Sequencing with the traffic already established, radio calls and the descent profile were managed without any prompt from the IP, above the desired levels for the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.
